headline: Parking ordinance 188-26 updating city parking rules recommended for adoption, as amended.
summary: The ordinance moves the parking clerk role into chapter 169, adds a process for temporary voter parking areas, and raises the senior parking pass fee to $10 from $5. Residential pass changes were set aside for later redrafting, and garage rate changes would need only a council vote. Separately, the council unanimously approved a home rule petition to let Fitchburg post legal notices on its website.
decisions: Approved renaming the Boulder Drive parking garage the Mill Street parking garage, 5-0.
Approved setting aside the changes to residential parking pass rules in subsection B of 169-54, 5-0.
Approved keeping the snow parking ban fine in group B, with no objection.
Recommended adoption of parking ordinance 188-26, as amended.
Approved supporting a home rule petition to allow digital posting of Fitchburg legal notices, unanimously.
discussion: Parking ordinance review: Members went through the changes section by section, covering meters, time limits, double parking, and voter parking. Some items were marked for later drafting, including the definitions of the off-street lots and garages.

Residential parking passes: Concerns were raised that passes for new downtown housing could take spaces near the senior center. Ideas included limiting passes to buildings of six units or fewer and barring them on Main Street and nearby side streets.
Garage rates: Members said the parking clerk would propose garage rates and the council would approve them by simple vote instead of by ordinance change.
Digital legal notices: Members said print notices cost the city money and reach few residents. Members said the petition would keep the same publication deadlines and record keeping requirements.
